questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What are proteins made of?
questions.solution: Proteins are polypeptides. They are linear chains of amino acids linked by peptide bonds.Each protein is a polymer of amino acids. As there are 20 types of amino acids (e.g., alanine, cysteine, proline, tryptophan, lysine, etc.), a protein is a heteropolymer and not a homopolymer. A homopolymer has only one type of monomer repeating ‘n’ number of times.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the common feature of all compounds found in the acid soluble pool?
options: They have molecular weights ranging from 18 to around 800 daltons
questions.solution: There is one feature common to all those compounds found in the acid soluble pool. They have molecular weights ranging from 18 to around 800 daltons (Da) approximately.The acid insoluble fraction, has only four types of organic compounds i.e., proteins, nucleic acids, polysaccharides and lipids. These classes of compounds with the exception of lipids, have molecular weights in the range of ten thousand daltons and above. For this very reason, biomolecules, i.e., chemical compounds found in living organisms are of two types. One, those which have molecular weights less than one thousand dalton and are usually referred to as micromolecules or simply biomolecules while those which are found in the acid insoluble fraction are called macromolecules or biomacromolecules.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Why are lipids considered part of the macromolecular fraction?
options: Because they are not strictly macromolecules
Because they are small molecular weight compounds
Because they are found in the acid soluble pool
Because they form structures like cell membranes and other membranes which get separated along with the acid insoluble pool
questions.solution: Lipids are indeed small molecular weight compounds and are present not only as such but also arranged into structures like cell membrane and other membranes. When we grind a tissue, we are disrupting the cell structure. Cell membrane and other membranes are broken into pieces, and form vesicles which are not water soluble. Therefore, these membrane fragments in the form of vesicles get separated along with the acid insoluble pool and hence in the macromolecular fraction. Lipids are not strictly macromolecules.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the acid soluble pool representative of?
options: The entire chemical composition of living tissues or organisms
The chemical composition of living tissue from abundance point of view
The macromolecules from cytoplasm and organelles
questions.solution: The acid soluble pool represents roughly the cytoplasmic composition. The macromolecules from cytoplasm and organelles become the acid insoluble fraction. Together they represent the entire chemical composition of living tissues or organisms. In summary if we represent the chemical composition of living tissue from abundance point of view and arrange them class-wise, we observe that water is the most abundant chemical in living organisms.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What are biomolecules commonly referred to as?
questions.solution: If one were to make a list of biomolecules, such a list would havethousands of organic compounds including amino acids, sugars, etc. For several reasons, we can call these biomolecules as ‘metabolites’. In animal tissues, one notices the presence of all such categories of compounds These are called primary metabolites. However, when one analyses plant, fungal and microbial cells, one would see thousands of compounds other than these called primary metabolites, e.g. alkaloids, flavonoids, rubber, essential oils, antibiotics, coloured pigments, scents, gums, spices. These are called secondary metabolites.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the difference between primary and secondary metabolites?
options: Primary metabolites have identifiable functions while secondary metabolites do not.
Secondary metabolites have identifiable functions while primary metabolites do not.
Both primary and secondary metabolites have identifiable functions.
Neither primary nor secondary metabolites have identifiable functions.
questions.solution: While primary metabolites have identifiable functions and play known roles in normal physiologial processes, we do not at the moment, understand the role or functions of all the ‘secondary metabolites’ in host organisms. However, many of them are useful to ‘human welfare’ (e.g., rubber, drugs, spices, scents and pigments). Some secondary metabolites have ecological importance.

The chemical and physical properties of amino acids are essentially

in solutions of different pH, the structure of amino acids changes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What type of elements are found in the ash?
questions.solution: One weighs a small amount of a living tissue (say a leaf or liver and this is called wet weight) and dry it. All the water, evaporates. The remaining material gives dry weight. Now if the tissue is fully burnt, all the carbon compounds are oxidised to gaseous form (CO2, water vapour) and are removed. What is remaining is called ‘ash’. This ash contains inorganic elements (like calcium, magnesium etc). Inorganic compounds like sulphate, phosphate, etc., are also seen in the acid-soluble fraction.

questions.q: What is the purpose of elemental analysis?
options: To determine the functional groups in living tissues
To determine the elemental composition of living tissues
To determine the organic and inorganic constituents in living tissues

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the purpose of extracting compounds from living tissues?
options: To isolate and purify a compound
To determine the molecular formula and structure
questions.solution: One extracts the compounds, then subjects the extract to various separation techniques till one has separated a compound from all other compounds. In other words, one isolates and purifies a compound. Analytical techniques, when applied to the compound give us an idea of the molecular formula and the probable structure of the compound. All the carbon compounds that we get from living tissues can be called ‘biomolecules’.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is obtained from straining the thick slurry obtained from grinding living tissue in trichloroacetic acid using a mortar and pestle?
options: Both the acid-soluble pool and the acid-insoluble fraction
questions.solution: We can take any living tissue (a vegetable or a piece of liver, etc.) and grind it in trichloroacetic acid (Cl3CCOOH) using a mortar and a pestle. We obtain a thick slurry. If we were to strain this through a cheesecloth or cotton we would obtain two fractions. One is called the filtrate or more technically, the acid-soluble pool, and the second, the retentate or the acid-insoluble fraction. Scientists have found thousands of organic compounds in the acid-soluble pool.

If we were to strain this through a cheesecloth or cotton we would obtain two fractions. One is called the filtrate or more technically, the acid-soluble pool, and the second, the retentate or the acid-insoluble fraction. Scientists have found thousands of organic compounds in the acid-soluble pool.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is an active site in an enzyme?
options: The pocket or crevice into which the substrate fits
questions.solution: The backbone of the protein chain folds upon itself, the chain criss-crosses itself and hence, many crevices or pockets are made. One such pocket is the ‘active site’. An active site of an enzyme is a crevice or pocket into which the substrate fits. Thus enzymes, through their active site, catalyse reactions at a high rate.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the difference between enzyme catalysts and inorganic catalysts?
options: Efficiency at high temperatures and pressures
Ability to retain catalytic power at high temperatures
Ability to work efficiently at high temperatures and high pressures
Resistance to damage at high temperatures
questions.solution: Enzyme catalysts differ from inorganic catalysts in many ways, but one major difference needs mention. Inorganic catalysts work efficiently at high temperatures and high pressures, while enzymes get damaged at high temperatures (say above 40°C). However, enzymes isolated from organisms who normally live under extremely high temperatures (e.g., hot vents and sulphur springs), are stable and retain their catalytic power even at high temperatures (upto 80°-90°C). Thermal stability is thus an important quality of such enzymes isolated from thermophilic organisms.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the formation of the ‘ES’ complex?

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the significance of the transition state structure?
options: It is the final structure of the product
It represents the highest energy state
It is a stable structural state
It is the structural transformation between substrate and product
questions.solution: The structure of substrate gets transformed into the structure of product(s). The pathway of this transformation must go through the so-called transition state structure. There could be many more ‘altered structural states’ between the stable substrate and the product. Implicit in this statement is the fact that all other intermediate structural states are unstable. Stability is something related to energy status of the molecule or the structure.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the energy required for the substrate to reach the transition state?
questions.solution: One need not supply energy (by heating) in order to form the product. However, whether it is an exothermic or spontaneous reaction or an endothermic or energy requiring reaction, the ‘S’ has to go through a much higher energy state or transition state. The difference in average energy content of ‘S’ from that of this transition state is called ‘activation energy’.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the effect of high temperatures on enzymes?
questions.solution: Enzymes generally function in a narrow range of temperature and pH (Figure 9.5). Each enzyme shows its highest activity at a particular temperature and pH called the optimum temperature and optimum pH. Activity declines both below and above the optimum value. Low temperature preserves the enzyme in a temporarily inactive state whereas high temperature destroys enzymatic activity because proteins are denatured by heat.

questions.solution: With the increase in substrate concentration, the velocity of the enzymatic reaction rises at first. The reaction ultimately reaches a maximum velocity (Vmax) which is not exceeded by any further rise in concentration of the substrate. This is because the enzyme molecules are fewer than the substrate molecules and after saturation of these molecules, there are no free enzyme molecules to bind with the additional substrate molecules

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is a competitive inhibitor?
options: An inhibitor that increases the activity of an enzyme
An inhibitor that decreases the activity of an enzyme
An inhibitor that does not affect the activity of an enzyme
questions.solution: When the inhibitor closely resembles the substrate in its molecular structure and inhibits the activity of the enzyme, it is known as competitive inhibitor. Due to its close structural similarity with the substrate, the inhibitor competes with the substrate for the substrate-binding site of the enzyme. Consequently, the substrate cannot bind and as a result, the enzyme action declines, e.g., inhibition of succinic dehydrogenase by malonate which closely resembles the substrate succinate in structure. Such competitive inhibitors are often used in the control of bacterial pathogens.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the function of cofactors in enzymes?
options: To make the enzyme catalytically active.
To tightly bind to the apoenzyme.
To catalyze the breakdown of water.
questions.solution: Enzymes are composed of one or several polypeptide chains. However, there are a number of cases in which non-protein constituents called co- factors are bound to the the enzyme to make the enzyme catalytically active. In these instances, the protein portion of the enzymes is called the apoenzyme. Three kinds of cofactors may be identified: prosthetic groups, co-enzymes and metal ions.

questions.subject: Botany

questions.solution: The other type of macromolecule that one would find in the acid insoluble fraction of any living tissue is the nucleic acid. These are polynucleotides. Together with polysaccharides and polypeptides these comprise the true macromolecular fraction of any living tissue or cell. For nucleic acids, the building block is a nucleotide. Nucleic acids serve as genetic material.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the function of polysaccharides in living systems?
options: Components of cell wall and storage forms of energy
questions.solution: Polysaccharides are components of cell wall in plants, fungi and also of the exoskeleton of arthropods. They also are storage forms of energy (e.g., starch and glycogen). Plant cell walls are made of cellulose. Paper made from plant pulp and cotton fibre is cellulosic. There are more complex polysaccharides in nature. They have as building blocks, amino-sugars and chemically modified sugars (e.g., glucosamine, N-acetyl galactosamine, etc.). Exoskeletons of arthropods, for example, have a complex polysaccharide called chitin. These complex polysaccharides are mostly homopolymers.

questions.q: Select the correct statement for the figure given below.
options: It gives us a 3-dimensional view of a protein.
The protein thread are folded into other forms like helix and pleated sheets is called the   tertiary structure.
In proteins, only right handed helices are observed.

questions.solution: Of course, only some portions of the protein thread are arranged in the form of a helix. In proteins, only right handed helices are observed. In addition, the long protein chain is also folded upon itself like a hollow woollen ball, giving rise to the tertiary structure (Fig.9.3c). This gives us a 3-dimensional view of a protein.

questions.q: What does the given figure represent?
options: These structures of protein are an assembly of more than one polypeptide or subunit.

The manner in which these individual folded polypeptides or subunits are arranged with respect to each other (e.g. linear string of spheres, spheres arranged one upon each other in the form of a cube or plate etc.) is called the quaternary structure of a protein.
Adult human haemoglobin is an example of quaternary structure of a protein.
Adult human haemoglobin consists of 4 subunits. Two of these are not identical to   each other.Two subunits of α type and two subunits of β type together constitute the human haemoglobin (Hb).
questions.solution: Some proteins are an assembly of more than one polypeptide or   subunits. The manner in which these individual folded polypeptides   or subunits are arranged with respect to each other (e.g. linear string   of spheres, spheres arranged one upon each other in the form of a   cube or plate etc.) is the architecture of a protein otherwise called   the quaternary structure of a protein (Fig. 9.3 d). Adult human   haemoglobin consists of 4 subunits. Two of these are identical to   each other. Hence, two subunits of α type and two subunits of β   type together constitute the human haemoglobin (Hb).

questions.solution: When the inhibitor closely resembles the substrate in its molecular structure and inhibits the activity of the enzyme, it is known as competitive inhibitor. questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the catalytic cycle of an enzyme action.

List-IList-II
A. Substrate bindingI. Breaks chemical bonds of the substrate
B. Induced fitII. Enzyme alters its shape to fit more tightly
C. Active site actionIII. Free enzyme is ready to bind to another molecule
D. End of cycleIV. Substrate fits into the active site

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
According to the catalytic cycle of an enzyme action described in NCERT:

First, the substrate binds to the active site of the enzyme, fitting into the active site (A-IV).

The binding of the substrate induces the enzyme to alter its shape, fitting more tightly around the substrate, which is known as induced fit (B-II).

The active site of the enzyme, now in close proximity to the substrate, breaks the chemical bonds of the substrate to form the enzyme-product complex (C-I).

Finally, the enzyme releases the products, and the free enzyme is ready to bind to another molecule of the substrate, marking the end of the cycle (D-III).

Therefore, the correct matching is A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III.

Answer: A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Consider the following biomolecules:
Alanine, Lecithin, Morphine, Ricin, Concanavalin A, Cholesterol, Curcumin

How many of the given biomolecules are classified as secondary metabolites?
questions.solution:
Primary metabolites have identifiable functions and play known roles in normal physiological processes. Alanine (an amino acid), lecithin (a phospholipid), and cholesterol (a lipid) are primary metabolites.

Secondary metabolites are products of certain metabolic pathways that do not have a known direct physiological role in the normal growth and development of the organism, but often have ecological importance or utility in human welfare. Morphine (alkaloid), ricin (toxin), concanavalin A (lectin), and curcumin (drug) are secondary metabolites.

Thus, there are exactly four secondary metabolites in the given list.

Answer: Four

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A linear oligosaccharide is composed exclusively of glucose units ($C_6H_{12}O_6$). If one molecule of this oligosaccharide contains exactly 31 oxygen atoms, how many glucose units are present in it?
questions.solution:
Let the number of glucose units in the linear oligosaccharide be $n$.

Each glucose monomer ($C_6H_{12}O_6$) contributes 6 oxygen atoms, giving an initial total of $6n$ oxygen atoms.

To link $n$ monomers in a linear chain, $(n-1)$ glycosidic bonds must be formed. Each glycosidic bond is formed via a dehydration reaction that releases one molecule of water ($H_2O$), thereby removing 1 oxygen atom.

The total number of oxygen atoms lost as water is $(n-1)$.

The final number of oxygen atoms in the oligosaccharide is $6n - (n-1) = 5n + 1$.

Given that the oligosaccharide contains 31 oxygen atoms:
$5n + 1 = 31$
$5n = 30$
$n = 6$

The oligosaccharide is a hexasaccharide containing 6 glucose units.

Option 2 is incorrect as it results from ignoring the water loss and simply dividing 31 by 6 to get an approximate integer.

Answer: 6

Therefore, both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding the catalytic cycle of enzyme action and the nature of enzyme-substrate interactions:

(A) The formation of the enzyme-substrate (ES) complex is an obligatory but transient phenomenon.
(B) Substrate binding induces the enzyme to alter its shape, forming a highly stable intermediate.
(C) The active site breaks the chemical bonds of the substrate to form the enzyme-product complex.
(D) The transition state structure is formed after the enzyme releases the products.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (A) is correct. According to NCERT, the formation of the ES complex is an obligatory and transient phenomenon during enzyme catalysis.

Statement (B) is incorrect. While substrate binding does induce the enzyme to alter its shape (induced fit), the intermediate transition state formed is unstable, not highly stable.

Statement (C) is correct. In the catalytic cycle, once the enzyme fits tightly around the substrate, the active site breaks the chemical bonds of the substrate to form the enzyme-product (EP) complex.

Statement (D) is incorrect. The transition state structure is formed while the substrate is bound to the enzyme's active site, long before the enzyme releases the products.

Therefore, exactly two statements ((A) and (C)) are correct.

Answer: Two

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: During the chemical analysis of a living tissue, it is dried and fully burnt to obtain 'ash'. Which of the following elements is recovered in this ash and has the highest percentage weight in the human body among the given options?
questions.solution:
When a living tissue is dried and fully burnt, all carbon compounds are oxidised to gaseous forms (such as $\text{CO}_{2}$ and water vapour) and escape. The remaining material, called ash, contains inorganic elements.

Because Carbon and Hydrogen escape as gases during burning, they are not recovered in the ash, eliminating them as correct choices despite their abundance in living tissue.

The ash retains inorganic elements like Calcium and Silicon. According to NCERT data on the elemental composition of the human body, Calcium constitutes $1.5\%$ of the body's weight, while Silicon is negligible.

Therefore, Calcium is the element recovered in the ash that has the highest percentage weight among the given options.

Answer: Calcium

Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution:

Despite all three molecules containing a carboxyl (acidic) group, they belong to different biochemical categories based on their core structures. On the other hand, amino acids are defined by having an amino group and an acidic (carboxyl) group as substituents on the same $\alpha$-carbon. Glutamic acid fits this structural definition and is thus classified as an amino acid.

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.q:
Read the following statements carefully:

(A) Metal ions form coordination bonds with side chains at the active site and at the same time form one or more coordination bonds with the substrate.
(B) Prosthetic groups are distinguished from other cofactors in that they bind transiently to the apoenzyme.
(C) Coenzymes are organic compounds whose essential chemical components are often vitamins.
(D) The catalytically active enzyme without its bound cofactor is called a holoenzyme.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (A) is correct as metal ions facilitate catalysis by forming coordination bonds with side chains at the active site and with the substrate.

Statement (B) is incorrect because prosthetic groups are distinguished by being tightly bound to the apoenzyme, whereas it is coenzymes that bind transiently.

Statement (C) is correct as the essential chemical components of many coenzymes are vitamins (e.g., NAD contains the vitamin niacin).

Statement (D) is incorrect because the catalytically active enzyme with its bound cofactor is called a holoenzyme. The enzyme without its cofactor is merely the protein portion, known as the apoenzyme.

Thus, exactly two statements (A and C) are correct.

Answer: Two

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Malonate is known to inhibit the activity of the enzyme succinic dehydrogenase. Which of the following statements most accurately describes the mechanism of this inhibition?
options: Malonate binds to a site other than the active site, altering the enzyme's conformation.
Malonate forms a covalent bond with the active site, causing irreversible inhibition.
Malonate structurally resembles the substrate succinate and competes for the substrate binding site of the enzyme.
Malonate closely resembles the enzyme in structure and competes for the substrate.
questions.solution:
The inhibition of succinic dehydrogenase by malonate is a classic example of competitive inhibition.

In competitive inhibition, the inhibitor closely resembles the substrate in its molecular structure. Malonate structurally resembles the actual substrate, succinate.

Due to this structural similarity, malonate competes with succinate for the substrate binding site (active site) of the enzyme, thereby blocking the enzyme's activity.

It does not bind to an allosteric site (which would be non-competitive inhibition), nor does it form irreversible covalent bonds or resemble the enzyme.

Answer: Malonate structurally resembles the substrate succinate and competes for the substrate binding site of the enzyme.

(B) Coenzyme(II) Zinc
(C) Metal ion(III) Apoenzyme
(D) Protein part of enzyme(IV) Haem

questions.solution:
The protein portion of enzymes is called the apoenzyme.

Prosthetic groups are organic compounds that are tightly bound to the apoenzyme. For example, in peroxidase and catalase, haem is the prosthetic group.

A number of enzymes require metal ions for their activity, which form coordination bonds with side chains at the active site. Zinc is a metal ion cofactor for carboxypeptidase.

Thus, the correct matching is (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(III).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Starch gives a characteristic blue colour when treated with iodine solution. Which of the following structural features of starch is responsible for this phenomenon?
options: It is a heteropolymer composed of multiple types of monosaccharides.
It forms covalent bonds with iodine molecules upon reaction.
It forms helical secondary structures that can hold iodine molecules.
It consists of highly branched chains without any secondary structure.
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, starch forms helical secondary structures. These helices act as a trap, holding the iodine ($I_2$) molecules inside the helical portion, which results in the characteristic blue colour.

Starch does not form covalent bonds with iodine, nor is it a heteropolymer (it is a homopolymer of glucose). While amylopectin in starch is branched, it is the presence of helical secondary structures that allows it to hold iodine.

Answer: It forms helical secondary structures that can hold iodine molecules.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A linear polysaccharide composed of 10 glucose ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6$) molecules has the chemical formula $\text{C}_{60}\text{H}_{102}\text{O}_{51}$.
Reason (R): In a polysaccharide chain, the right end is called the reducing end and the left end is called the non-reducing end.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct. A linear polysaccharide of 10 glucose molecules will have 9 glycosidic bonds. Since each bond formation releases one water molecule ($\text{H}_2\text{O}$), 9 water molecules ($\text{H}_{18}\text{O}_9$) are lost.
Total atoms before dehydration: $10 \times \text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6 = \text{C}_{60}\text{H}_{120}\text{O}_{60}$.
After subtracting 9 water molecules: $\text{C}_{60}\text{H}_{120}\text{O}_{60} - \text{H}_{18}\text{O}_9 = \text{C}_{60}\text{H}_{102}\text{O}_{51}$.

Reason (R) is also correct. According to NCERT, in a polysaccharide chain (like glycogen), the right end is the reducing end and the left end is the non-reducing end.

However, (R) does not explain (A). The correct explanation for (A) would be the loss of 9 water molecules during the formation of 9 glycosidic bonds.

Therefore, both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: When a living tissue is ground in trichloroacetic acid and filtered, various biomolecules separate into acid-soluble and acid-insoluble fractions. Which of the following secondary metabolites will be recovered in the acid-insoluble fraction and is classified as a polymeric substance?
questions.solution:
Biomolecules that have molecular weights strictly in the range of 18 to 800 Daltons are found in the acid-soluble pool, while macromolecules (proteins, nucleic acids, polysaccharides) are found in the acid-insoluble fraction (retentate).

Cellulose is a polysaccharide, making it a macromolecule that will be found in the acid-insoluble fraction. Furthermore, it is explicitly classified under 'Polymeric substances' in the secondary metabolites table.

Concanavalin A is a protein (macromolecule) and thus acid-insoluble, but it is classified as a lectin, not a polymeric substance.
Curcumin is classified as a drug and Anthocyanin as a pigment; both are micromolecules found in the acid-soluble pool.

Answer: Cellulose

Reason (R): Malonate closely resembles the substrate succinate in its molecular structure, allowing it to compete for the active site.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation for Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation for Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is incorrect.
Assertion (A) is incorrect but Reason (R) is correct.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct because malonate is a well-known competitive inhibitor of the enzyme succinic dehydrogenase.

Reason (R) is also correct and provides the exact mechanism for this inhibition. Competitive inhibitors function by structurally resembling the substrate. Malonate closely resembles the substrate succinate, which allows it to bind to the active site of succinic dehydrogenase, thereby competing with the actual substrate and inhibiting the enzyme's activity.

Thus, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation for Assertion (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation for Assertion (A).

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In an enzyme-catalysed reaction, the velocity ultimately reaches a maximum value ($V_{max}$) which is not exceeded by any further rise in substrate concentration.
Reason (R): At high substrate concentrations, there are no free substrate molecules left to bind with the active sites of the enzyme.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct because the velocity of an enzyme-catalysed reaction rises initially with an increase in substrate concentration and then levels off at a maximum velocity ($V_{max}$).

Reason (R) is incorrect. The plateau occurs because enzyme molecules are typically fewer in number than substrate molecules. At high substrate concentrations, all the active sites of the enzyme are saturated. Therefore, there are no free enzyme molecules (not substrate molecules) left to bind with the additional substrate molecules.

Answer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements carefully:

(A) The protein portion of the enzymes is called the apoenzyme.
(B) Prosthetic groups are distinguished from other cofactors in that they are tightly bound to the apoenzyme.
(C) Coenzymes serve as co-factors in a number of different enzyme catalysed reactions and bind tightly to the apoenzyme.
(D) Catalytic activity is retained when the co-factor is removed from the holoenzyme.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (A) is correct: In conjugated enzymes, the protein portion is called the apoenzyme.

Statement (B) is correct: Prosthetic groups are organic compounds that are distinguished from other cofactors by their tight binding to the apoenzyme.

Statement (C) is incorrect: Coenzymes are organic compounds whose association with the apoenzyme is only transient, usually occurring during the course of catalysis. They do not bind tightly.

Statement (D) is incorrect: Catalytic activity is lost when the co-factor is removed from the enzyme, proving its crucial role in catalysis.

Therefore, exactly two statements ((A) and (B)) are correct.

Answer: Two

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
In a standard graph of the velocity of an enzyme-catalysed reaction (y-axis) against substrate concentration (x-axis), the curve obtained is a rectangular hyperbola. The horizontal asymptote of this curve is denoted by 'P'. The value on the y-axis corresponding to exactly half of 'P' is denoted by 'Q'. The corresponding value on the x-axis that yields a velocity of 'Q' is denoted by 'R'.

Identify the kinetic parameters represented by P, Q, and R.
questions.solution:
In the graph of enzyme reaction velocity (v) versus substrate concentration (S), the curve is a rectangular hyperbola.

The velocity reaches a maximum limit which is represented by the horizontal asymptote. Thus, P represents the maximum velocity, $V_{max}$.

Q is exactly half of this maximum velocity on the y-axis, so Q represents $\dfrac{V_{max}}{2}$.

The substrate concentration on the x-axis at which the reaction velocity is half of its maximum value ($\dfrac{V_{max}}{2}$) is known as the Michaelis constant ($K_{m}$). Therefore, R represents $K_{m}$.

Answer: P = $V_{max}$, Q = $\dfrac{V_{max}}{2}$, R = $K_{m}$

Read the following statements regarding lipids:

Statement I: The R group in a fatty acid could be a methyl, ethyl or higher number of $-\text{CH}_{2}$ groups (1 carbon to 19 carbons).
Statement II: Palmitic acid has 16 carbons excluding the carboxyl carbon.
Statement III: Arachidonic acid has 20 carbon atoms including the carboxyl carbon.
Statement IV: Oils have higher melting points than fats and hence remain as oil in winters.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement I is correct; the R group in fatty acids can range from 1 to 19 carbons.

Statement II is incorrect; palmitic acid has 16 carbons including the carboxyl carbon, not excluding it.

Statement III is correct; arachidonic acid has 20 carbon atoms including the carboxyl carbon.

Statement IV is incorrect; oils have lower melting points (e.g., gingelly oil) compared to fats, which is why they remain liquid in winter.

Thus, exactly two statements (I and III) are correct.

Answer: Only two

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion and the other is labelled as Reason.

Assertion: All the elements present in a sample of Earth's crust are also present in a sample of living tissue.
Reason: The relative abundance of carbon and hydrogen with respect to other elements is lower in any living organism than in Earth's crust.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is correct but Reason is not correct.
Assertion is not correct but Reason is correct.
questions.solution:
Assertion is correct: When elemental analysis is performed on a piece of Earth's crust and a living tissue, we obtain a similar list of elements. In absolute terms, all the elements present in a sample of Earth's crust are also present in a sample of living tissue.

Reason is incorrect: A closer examination reveals that the relative abundance of carbon and hydrogen with respect to other elements is higher (not lower) in any living organism than in Earth's crust.

Therefore, the Assertion is correct but the Reason is not correct.

Answer: Assertion is correct but Reason is not correct.

questions.q: Enzymes catalysing the linking together of two compounds, for example, enzymes which catalyse joining of C-O, C-S, C-N, P-O etc., bonds are classified as :
questions.solution:
Ligases are the class of enzymes that catalyse the linking together of two compounds, e.g., enzymes which catalyse joining of C-O, C-S, C-N, P-O etc. bonds.

Lyases catalyse the removal of groups by mechanisms other than hydrolysis leaving double bonds.

Transferases catalyse a transfer of a group (other than hydrogen) between a pair of substrates.

Hydrolases catalyse the hydrolysis of ester, ether, peptide, glycosidic, C-C, C-halide or P-N bonds.

Answer: Ligases

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following acts as the prosthetic group in the enzymes peroxidase and catalase that catalyse the breakdown of hydrogen peroxide?
questions.solution:
In enzymes like peroxidase and catalase, which catalyse the breakdown of hydrogen peroxide to water and oxygen, haem is the prosthetic group and it is a part of the active site of the enzyme.

Zinc is a metal ion cofactor for the proteolytic enzyme carboxypeptidase.

Niacin is a vitamin that forms an essential chemical component of the coenzymes NAD and NADP.

Flavin is associated with other coenzymes like FAD, not as the prosthetic group of catalase.

Answer: Haem

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Identify the competitive inhibitor of the enzyme succinic dehydrogenase and the specific substrate it structurally resembles, respectively.
questions.solution:
The enzyme succinic dehydrogenase acts on its normal substrate, succinate.

Malonate acts as a competitive inhibitor of this enzyme because its molecular structure closely resembles that of succinate. Due to this structural similarity, malonate competes with succinate for the substrate binding site of the enzyme.

Thus, the competitive inhibitor is malonate and the substrate it resembles is succinate. Reversing the order or confusing malonate with malate leads to incorrect choices.

Answer: Malonate and Succinate

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II regarding enzyme kinetics.

List-IList-II
A. $V_{\text{max}}$I. Velocity rises steeply with increase in substrate concentration
B. $K_m$II. Substrate concentration at half-maximal velocity
C. Initial phaseIII. Maximum velocity achieved by the reaction
D. Saturation phaseIV. All enzyme active sites are occupied and no free enzyme is available

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
$V_{\text{max}}$ represents the maximum velocity achieved by the reaction when all enzyme active sites are saturated.

$K_m$ (Michaelis constant) is defined as the substrate concentration at which the reaction velocity is half of $V_{\text{max}}$.

During the initial phase of the reaction, the velocity rises steeply as substrate concentration increases.

In the saturation phase, the reaction velocity does not increase further because all enzyme active sites are occupied by substrate molecules and no free enzyme is available.

Therefore, the correct match is A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV.

Answer: A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).



Assertion (A): Chitin, found in the exoskeletons of arthropods, is a complex polysaccharide.



Reason (R): Chitin is a heteropolymer made up of chemically modified sugars such as N-acetyl glucosamine.



In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct because chitin is indeed a complex polysaccharide found in the exoskeletons of arthropods.



Reason (R) is incorrect. Although chitin is made up of chemically modified sugars (N-acetyl glucosamine), NCERT specifies that these complex polysaccharides are mostly homopolymers, not heteropolymers. A homopolymer consists of only one type of monomer repeating throughout the chain.



Thus, (A) is correct but (R) is not correct.



Answer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Complete hydrolysis of a certain macromolecule isolated from plant tissue yields only fructose molecules. Identify the macromolecule and the specific type of bond that is broken during this process.
questions.solution:
The macromolecule that yields only fructose upon complete hydrolysis is inulin, which is a homopolymer of fructose found in plants.

Because inulin is a polysaccharide, its monosaccharide monomers (fructose) are linked together by glycosidic bonds. Hydrolysis of inulin involves the breaking of these glycosidic bonds.

Insulin is a protein hormone (linked by peptide bonds) and yields amino acids. Cellulose yields glucose. Phosphodiester bonds are found in nucleic acids.

Answer: Inulin and glycosidic bond

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Three molecules of glucose ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6$) are linked together to form a linear trisaccharide. What is the chemical formula of the resulting trisaccharide?
questions.solution:
A linear trisaccharide is formed by linking three monosaccharide units, which requires the formation of two glycosidic bonds.

The formation of each glycosidic bond involves a dehydration reaction (removal of one water molecule, $\text{H}_2\text{O}$). Thus, two water molecules ($\text{H}_4\text{O}_2$) are removed in total.

Total atoms before dehydration: $3 \times \text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6 = \text{C}_{18}\text{H}_{36}\text{O}_{18}$

Subtracting two water molecules: $\text{C}_{18}\text{H}_{36}\text{O}_{18} - \text{H}_4\text{O}_2 = \text{C}_{18}\text{H}_{32}\text{O}_{16}$

Therefore, the correct formula is $\text{C}_{18}\text{H}_{32}\text{O}_{16}$.

Answer: $\text{C}_{18}\text{H}_{32}\text{O}_{16}$

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): During the catalytic cycle, the active site of the enzyme breaks the chemical bonds of the substrate.

Reason (R): The binding of the substrate induces the enzyme to alter its shape, bringing the active site in close proximity to the substrate.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true. In the catalytic cycle, the active site of the enzyme breaks the chemical bonds of the substrate to form the new enzyme-product complex.

Reason (R) is true. The binding of the substrate induces the enzyme to alter its shape (induced fit), fitting more tightly around the substrate.

Reason (R) is the correct explanation for Assertion (A). It is precisely this induced alteration in shape that brings the active site into close proximity with the substrate, enabling it to effectively break the chemical bonds.

Therefore, both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements carefully:
(A) Coenzymes are organic compounds that are tightly bound to the apoenzyme.
(B) The essential chemical components of many coenzymes are vitamins.
(C) Zinc is a cofactor for the proteolytic enzyme carboxypeptidase.
(D) The non-protein constituents bound to the enzyme to make it catalytically active are called apoenzymes.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (A) is incorrect because coenzymes are organic compounds whose association with the apoenzyme is only transient, usually occurring during the course of catalysis. Prosthetic groups are the ones that are tightly bound.

Statement (B) is correct as the essential chemical components of many coenzymes are vitamins (e.g., NAD and NADP contain the vitamin niacin).

Statement (C) is correct as zinc acts as a cofactor for the proteolytic enzyme carboxypeptidase.

Statement (D) is incorrect because the non-protein constituents bound to the enzyme are called cofactors, whereas the protein portion of the enzyme is called the apoenzyme.

Therefore, exactly two statements, (B) and (C), are correct.

Answer: Two

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In a laboratory experiment, the rate of conversion of succinate to fumarate by the enzyme succinate dehydrogenase is measured. The concentration of the enzyme is kept constant while the concentration of the substrate, succinate, is progressively increased from a very low level to a very high level. Which of the following best describes the expected trend in the velocity of this reaction?
options: The velocity increases indefinitely in direct proportion to the succinate concentration.
The velocity increases initially but eventually plateaus at a maximum value.
The velocity increases to a peak and then declines as succinate concentration becomes too high.
The velocity remains constant from the beginning regardless of the succinate concentration.
questions.solution:
Succinate dehydrogenase is an enzyme and follows standard enzyme saturation kinetics. With an increase in substrate (succinate) concentration, the velocity of the enzymatic reaction rises steeply at first.

However, the reaction ultimately reaches a maximum velocity ($V_{\text{max}}$) which is not exceeded by any further rise in the concentration of the substrate. This occurs because the number of enzyme molecules is fixed and fewer than the substrate molecules at high concentrations.

Once all the active sites of the enzyme molecules are saturated with succinate, there are no free enzyme molecules to bind the additional substrate, causing the velocity to plateau. It does not decline at high substrate concentrations (unlike the effect of extreme temperature or pH), nor does it increase indefinitely.

Answer: The velocity increases initially but eventually plateaus at a maximum value.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A triglyceride molecule is synthesized by the esterification of one molecule of glycerol ($C_3H_8O_3$) with three molecules of palmitic acid ($C_{16}H_{32}O_2$). What is the total number of oxygen atoms present in one molecule of the resulting triglyceride?
questions.solution:
One molecule of glycerol contains 3 oxygen atoms.

Three molecules of palmitic acid contain $3 \times 2 = 6$ oxygen atoms.

The total number of oxygen atoms before the reaction is $3 + 6 = 9$.

During the formation of a triglyceride, three ester bonds are formed between the hydroxyl groups of glycerol and the carboxyl groups of the fatty acids. This dehydration synthesis releases three molecules of water ($H_2O$).

Since each water molecule contains 1 oxygen atom, a total of 3 oxygen atoms are removed during the process.

The final number of oxygen atoms in the triglyceride is $9 - 3 = 6$.

Option 2 is incorrect because it fails to subtract the oxygen lost as water. Option 1 is incorrect because it subtracts only one water molecule instead of three.

Answer: 6

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: During an enzyme-catalysed reaction, it is observed that the binding of the substrate has just induced the enzyme to alter its shape, fitting more tightly around the substrate. According to the catalytic cycle of enzyme action, what is the immediate next step?
options: The substrate binds to the active site of the enzyme.
The active site breaks the chemical bonds of the substrate to form the enzyme-product complex.
The enzyme releases the products of the reaction.
The free enzyme is ready to bind to another molecule of the substrate.
questions.solution:
The catalytic cycle of an enzyme action proceeds in a specific sequence:
1. First, the substrate binds to the active site of the enzyme.
2. The binding of the substrate induces the enzyme to alter its shape, fitting more tightly around the substrate.
3. The active site of the enzyme, now in close proximity to the substrate, breaks the chemical bonds of the substrate and the new enzyme-product complex is formed.
4. The enzyme releases the products of the reaction and the free enzyme is ready to bind to another molecule of the substrate.

The scenario described in the question corresponds to step 2. Therefore, the immediate next step is step 3, where the active site breaks the chemical bonds of the substrate to form the enzyme-product complex.

Answer: The active site breaks the chemical bonds of the substrate to form the enzyme-product complex.

questions.q: Which of the following graphs depicts the effect of substrate concentration on velocity of enzyme catalysed reaction?
questions.solution:
Option (1) is the correct answer because with the increase in substrate concentration, the velocity of enzymatic reaction rises at first. The reaction ultimately reaches maximum velocity $\left(\mathrm{V}_{\max }\right)$ which is not exceeded by any further rise in concentration of the substrate. This is because the enzyme molecules are fewer than substrate molecules and after saturation of these molecules, there are no free enzyme molecules to bind the additional substrate molecules

Option (2) is incorrect as velocity of reaction is continuously increasing in the given graph.
In option (3) after reaching at $\mathrm{V}_{\text{max }}$, velocity declines while in option (4) velocity of reaction declines from high on increasing substrate concentration. So, option (3) and (4) are incorrect.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Regarding catalytic cycle of an enzyme action, select the correct sequential steps :
A. Substrate enzyme complex formation.
B. Free enzyme ready to bind with another substrate.
C. Release of products.
D. Chemical bonds of the substrate broken.
E. Substrate binding to active site.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option (4) which is E, A, D, C, B.
The catalytic cycle of an enzyme action can be described in the following steps.
(1) The binding of the substrate induces the enzyme to alter its shape, fitting more tightly around the substrate.
(2) The active site of the enzyme, now in close proximity of the substrate breaks the chemical bonds of the substrate and the new enzyme-product complex is formed.
(3) The enzyme releases the products of the reaction and the free enzyme is ready to bind to another molecule of the substrate and run through the catalytic cycle once again.
(4) First, the substrate binds to the active site of the enzyme, fitting into the active site.

Options (1), (2) and (3) are incorrect as the steps mentioned are in the wrong sequence.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Malonate inhibits the growth of pathogenic bacteria by inhibiting the activity of:
questions.solution:
The activity of any enzyme is extremely sensitive to the presence of specific chemicals that bind to the enzyme. Inhibitors are capable of switching off the activity of enzyme.

When the inhibitor closely resembles the substrate in its molecular structure and inhibits the activity of the enzyme, it is known as competitive inhibitor. Competitive inhibitors compete with the substrate for the substrate binding site of the enzyme and block the activity.

The inhibition of succinic dehydrogenase enzyme by malonate which closely resembles the substrate succinate in structure is an example of competitive inhibition.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Identify the basic amino acid from the following.
questions.solution:
Amino acids based on a number of NH2 and COOH groups can be classified into three types:

Neutral amino acids: The amino acids having an equal number of amino and carboxyl groups are called neutral amino acids. E.g. Glycine, alanine, valine, leucine, isoleucine, proline, methionine, tryptophan, phenylalanine, serine, threonine, cysteine, asparagine, glutamine, and tyrosine.

Acidic amino acids: The amino acids having more carboxyl groups as compared to amine groups are called acidic or negative amino acids. E.g. Aspartic acid and glutamic acid.

Basic amino acids: The amino acids having more amine groups as compared to carboxyl groups are called basic or negative amino acids. E.g. Lysine, arginine, and histidine.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
$( A )$ Coenzyme or metal ion that is tightly bound to enzyme protein is called prosthetic group.
$( B )$ A complete catalytic active enzyme with its bound prosthetic group is called apoenzyme.
Select the correct option.
options: Both $( A )$ and $( B )$ are correct.
$( A )$ is true but $( B )$ is false.
Both $( A )$ and $( B )$ are false.
$( A )$ is false but $( B )$ is true
questions.solution: Many enzymes show catalytic activity only in association with certain non-protein substances. Those substances are known as cofactors (cofactors may be simple metal ions, e.g. Mg++ or K+ etc.). The enzymes which works only in presence of cofactors are called apoenzymes. An organic non-protein cofactor which is easily separable from the apoenzyme is called coenzyme, and the non-protein organic cofactor that is tightly bound to and non-dissociable from the enzyme is termed as prosthetic group, e.g. biotin of carboxylases, haem of hemoglobin, etc.

questions.q: The two functional groups characteristic of sugars are
questions.solution:
Monosaccharides can be further classified by their most highly oxidized functional group. Sugars are chemically carbohydrates. They are polyhydroxy aldehydes ketones and their condensation products. Aldoses bear a terminal aldehyde or -CHO group while ketoses have an internal ketone or -CO group.
Thus, they possess two functional groups, i.e. carbonyl and hydroxyl.

questions.q: Which of the following is the least likely to be involved in stabilizing the three-dimensional folding of most proteins?
questions.solution:
Tertiary structure: The overall shape of a protein molecule; and the spatial relationship of the secondary structures to one another; is called the tertiary structure of the protein. In other words, the various folds which give three-dimensional appearances to protein form its tertiary structure. This structure is stabilised by the various bonds like hydrogen bond, disulphide bond, electrostatic bond, hydrophobic bonds, Van der Waals forces and peptide bond.

An ester bond is formed between sugar and phosphate in a nucleotide. DNA and RNA are composed of nucleotides that are linked to one another in a chain by chemical bonds, called ester bonds, between the sugar base of one nucleotide and the phosphate group of the adjacent nucleotide. This bond is least likely to be involved in stabilizing of the protein.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following statements is incorrect?
options: A competitive inhibitor reacts reversibly with the enzyme to form an enzyme-inhibitor complex.
In competitive inhibition, the inhibitor molecule is not chemically changed by the enzyme.
The competitive inhibitor does not affect the rate of breakdown of the enzyme-substrate complex.
The presence of the competitive inhibitor decreases the Km of the enzyme for the substrate.
questions.solution: Competitive inhibition is a form of enzyme inhibition where binding of the inhibitor to the active site on the enzyme prevents binding of the substrate and vice versa. The presence of a competitive inhibitor increases the Km constant of the enzyme (and not decrease), while it does not affect the Vmax. The competitive inhibitor binds at the active site, so decreases the affinity of the enzyme for its substrate, so Km constant increases. If substrate concentration is increased, inhibition overcomes and attains normal Vmax.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following is a non-reducing carbohydrate?
questions.solution: A reducing sugar is any sugar that is capable of acting as a reducing agent because it has a free aldehyde group or a free ketone group. All monosaccharides are reducing sugars, along with some disaccharides, oligosaccharides, and polysaccharides. The monosaccharides can be divided into two groups: the aldoses, which have an aldehyde group, and the ketoses, which have a ketone group. Ketoses must first tautomerize to aldoses before they can act as reducing sugars. The common dietary monosaccharides are galactose, glucose and fructose are all reducing sugars. Sucrose is a disaccharide. It is composed of each one of the glucose and fructose molecules joined together by $\alpha - 1,2$ glycosidic bond. It is an example of non-reducing sugars.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about enzymes is wrong?
options: Enzymes are denatured at high temperatures.
Enzymes are mostly proteins but some are lipids also.
Enzymes require optimum $\mathrm{pH}$ and temperature for maximum activity.
questions.solution:
Chemically, enzymes are generally globular proteins. Enzymes are catalysts that breakdown or synthesize more complex chemical compounds. They speed up the rate of chemical reactions because they lower the energy of activation, the energy that must be supplied in order for molecules to react with one another. Anything that an enzyme normally combines with is called a substrate. Enzymes are very efficient. Enzymes are only present in small amounts in the cell since they are not altered during their reactions. and they are highly specific for their substrate. Each enzyme has an optimum temperature and $\mathrm{pH}$ at which it works best. However, at much higher temperature, they are denatured.

questions.solution: The amount of energy required to raise the energy of molecules at which chemical reaction can occur is called activation energy. questions.q: A competitive inhibitor of succinic dehydrogenase is
questions.solution:
Succinic dehydrogenase oxidised the succinate to fumarate. In eukaryotes succinate dehydrogenase is tightly bound to the inner mitochondrial membrane, in prokaryotes to the plasma membrane. Electrons pass from succinate through the FAD and iron-sulphur centres before entering the chain of electron carriers in the mitochondrial inner membrane Malonate, an analogue of succinate is a strong competitive inhibitor of succinate dehydrogenase and therefore, blocks the activity of citric acid cycle.
In Krebs cycle the reversible hydration of fumarate to malate is catalysed by fumarase enzyme.
In the last reaction of Krebs cycle NAD-linked L-malate dehydrogenase catalyses the oxidation of L-malate to oxaloacetate. The isocitrate dehydrogenase in Krebs cycle catalyses oxidative decarboxylation of isocitrate to form $\alpha$-ketoglutarate, which in next step through oxidative decarboxylation converted to succinyl Co-A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following statements regarding enzyme inhibition is correct?
options: competitive inhibition is seen when a substrate competes with an enzyme for binding to an inhibitor protein
competitive inhibition is seen when the substrate and the inhibitor compete for the active site on the enzyme
non-competitive inhibition of an enzyme can be overcome by adding large amount of substrate
non-competitive inhibitors often bind to the enzyme irreversibly.
questions.solution: Competitive Inhibition occurs when the binding of the inhibitor to the active site on the enzyme prevents the binding of the substrate and vice versa. The binding of competitive inhibitors to enzymes are reversible. Non-competitive inhibition occurs when the inhibitor binds to the enzyme at a site away from the active site such that even on binding of the substrate, the enzyme functions less effectively. This type of inhibition is reversible and cannot be overcome by adding a large amount of substrate. Related Theory Enzyme inhibitors prevent the formation of an enzyme-substrate complex and hence prevent the formation of product. Inhibition of enzymes may be either reversible or irreversible depending on the specific effect of the inhibitor being used. Competitive inhibition involves a molecule, other than the substrate, binding to the enzyme's active site. The molecule (inhibitor) is structurally and chemically similar to the substrate and hence able to bind to the active site. The competitive inhibitor blocks the active site and thus prevents substrate binding. As the inhibitor is in competition with the substrate, its effects can be reduced by increasing substrate concentration. Non-competitive inhibition involves a molecule binding to $a$ site other than the active site (an allosteric site). (Ref. to Fig. 27.3)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: During prolonged fastings, in what sequence are the following organic compounds used up by the body ?
options: first carbohydrates, next fats and lastly proteins
first fats, next carbohydrates and lastly proteins
first carbohydrates, next proteins and lastly lipids
first proteins, next lipids and lastly carbohydrates
questions.solution: During prolonged fasting, first carbohydrates are used up then fats and proteins are used last. Carbohydrate and fat metabolism can produce energy more easily than protein and they follow a more or less simple pathway to enter into TCA cycle. When all carbohydrates of the body are used up then fats are converted into carbohydrates and when all fats are used up then ultimately proteins of the body are converted into carbohydrates to be used up by the body.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one is a reducing sugar?
questions.solution:
All those carbohydrates which contain a free aldehyde or ketonic group and reduce Fehling's solution and Tollen's reagent are referred as a reducing sugar. Examples of reducing sugar are galactose, glucose, glyceraldehyde, fructose, ribose, and xylose.
Non-reducing sugars do not have an $\mathrm{OH}$ group attached to the anomeric carbon so they cannot reduce other compounds. All monosaccharides such as glucose are reducing sugars. Examples Sucrose, Trehalose, Raffinose, Stachyose.
A Caution
$\Rightarrow$ The anomeric carbon is the carbon derived from the carbonyl carbon compound (the ketone or aldehyde functional group) of the open-chain form of the carbohydrate molecule. The anomeric carbon can be determined by the carbon attached to two oxygen atoms joined by single bonds.

It further brings new stearic relationships of amino acids specially those which are far apart in the linear sequence. Tertiary structure is stabilized by several types of bonds - hydrogen bonds, ionic bonds, van der Waal's interactions, covalent bonds, hydrophobic bonds. Tertiary structure gives the protein a three dimensional conformation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Assertion : Enzymes lower down the activation energy of the reactant molecule to make its transition into product easier.
Reason : Enzymes are highly substrate specific catalysts.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: Enzymes are highly substrate specific i.e. they catalyze the reaction of a particular substrate only. They facilitate occurrence of a reaction and transition of reactant into product. A chemical reaction $S \rightarrow P$ (where $S$ is the substrate and $P$ the product or products) will take place when a certain number of $S$ molecules at any given instant possess enough energy to attain an activated condition called the 'transition state'. The enzyme combines transiently with the substrate to produce a transient state having a lower energy of activation than that of substrate alone. This results in acceleration of the reaction. Once the products are formed, the enzyme (or catalyst) is free or regenerated to combine with another molecule of the substrate and repeat the process.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Assertion : Glycerides are important nutrients for body.
Reason : Glycerides are hydrolysed into glycerol and fatty acids which are further absorbed in intestine by the formation of chylomicron.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution:
Glycerides, mainly triglycerides are a principle form of fats present in our food. During digestion, fats are digested to form monoglycerides and free fatty acids. They first become dissolved in the central lipid portions of bile micelles which are soluble in chyme. In this form, the monoglycerides and free fatty acids are carried to the surfaces of the microvilli of the intestinal cell brush border and then penetrate into the interior of the epithelial cells, which is possible because the lipids are also soluble in the epithelial cell membrane. This leaves the bile micelles still in the chyme, where they function again and to help absorb still more monoglycerides and fatty acids.
After entering the epithelial cell, the fatty acids and monoglycerides are taken up by the cell's smooth endoplasmic reticulum; here they are mainly used to form new triglycerides that are subsequently released in the form of chylomicrons through the base of the epithelial cell, to flow upward through the thoracic lymph duct and empty into the circulating blood. Thus, chylomicrons help in transport of glycerides through blood circulation to various body parts.

questions.explanation:
The enzyme complex (holoenzyme) is made up of two parts i.e., protein part (apoenzyme) and non-protein part (cofactor). Cofactor is of three types -
(i) prosthetic group
(ii) coenzymes
(iii) metal ions

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The basic unit of chitin is
questions.solution: The chitin (= polyglycosamine) is an acetate of mucopolysaccharide called glycosamine which is formed by the combination of polysaccharide with small peptide molecules. The basic unit (monomer) of chitin is $N$-acetylglucosamine, monomers are joined by $1-4 \beta$ linkages.
